title: tempo-release-conductor-ops-chef-notes-and-shift-scripts-nov-2026-wip
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact conductor-style runbook for small-to-medium weekend cutovers where we want a tight, staggered cadence (the ‘tempo’ plan) rather than a full-blown marathon run. It bundles operator shift scripts, comm templates, telemetry gates, and a tiny smoke-test harness that can be run from a laptop if the console is degraded.

Audience:
- Release shepherds and on-call SREs
- Release engineers running the cutover
- Solutions eng and SEs on standby for customer-impacting flows

Status and intent:
- WIP: field-tested in a dry-run on 2026-10-22; lessons from that run are annotated below.
- This doc deliberately prioritizes brevity and checklist clarity over exhaustive explanation. Use linked artifacts for longer background.

High-level rhythm (tempo):
- T-180m: final preflight checks (team sync, ticket gating, toggle plan)
- T-60m: stage smoke + read-only validation in staging mirror (parallel teams)
- T-30m: final thumbs up from telemetry gate owners (latency/cpu/queue depth OK)
- T=0: cutover start (traffic ramp rules applied)
- T+15m: initial service-level smoke tests and canary sampling (5-10% traffic)
- T+45m: increment to 50% if metrics stable, otherwise hold/rollback
- T+90m: promote to 100% or rollback based on policy

Contact and channels (quick):
- Primary Slack channel: #cutover-ops (pinned: checklist, playbook link, broadcast templates)
- Incident bridge: +1-650-555-0111 (zoom id: 823-111-220)
- Pager on-call: eng-sre-primary

Preflight checklist (T-180m -> T-60m):
- Owner: release lead (assign if not already done)
- Confirm release artifact sha and manifest (manifest URL in linked artifacts)
- Validate schema migration plan exists and has rollback script (if applicable)
- Verify capacity headroom in target region(s) (>= 30% spare for surge)
- Confirm feature flags and controlled toggles (list flags and their safe defaults)
- Run quick diff of infra Terraform plan in dry-run mode: terraform plan -var-file=release.vars
- Ensure monitoring dashboards are up and dashboards for this cutover are pinned in #cutover-ops
- Confirm on-call rotations for next 6 hours (who handles what). Put names in Slack.

Telemetry gate definitions (T-60m -> T+90m):
- Latency P50/P95/P99 should not exceed baseline + 20/30/50% respectively in canary window.
- Error rate (5xx or service-specific) must remain <= baseline + 0.5 percentage points.
- Queue depth (inference work queue) must remain below 2x baseline or a hard cap of 2000 waiting items.
- GPU memory OOMs or GPU scheduling spikes: immediate abort.
- Any customer-facing 500s for a VIP customer: immediate hold + notify customer success.

Pre-cutover manual smoke (T-60m):
- Run quick functional script from laptop (if internal network allows) against staging mirror:
  ./scripts/smoke-run.sh --endpoint https://staging-mirror.redwood-inference.internal --profile small-load
- Expected output: no auth failures, sample generations <= 1200 ms median, embeddings match golden set for 5/5 samples.
- If any step fails, escalate to release lead and pause. Document failure in #cutover-ops with at least one console screenshot and logs link.

Cutover step-by-step (T-0 onward):
1) Announce T-0 in #cutover-ops and to engineering-general for visibility (use broadcast template).
2) Apply routing policy change (infra CLI): rcli apply-route --plan release-2026-11-tempo.json --stagger 15m
3) Start canary (5% traffic): rcli promote --subset canary --percent 5 --note "tempo-run by <owner>"
4) Wait 15 minutes. Run smoke tests and snapshot key metrics (see smoke template below).
5) Evaluate telemetry gates. If pass, move to 50%; if fail, execute rollback matrix.
6) At 50%, hold for 30 minutes with automated rate-limited increases disabled. Repeat telemetry.
7) If all gates healthy, promote to 100% and monitor 60 more minutes before declaring done.

Quick smoke template (run at T+15m and T+45m):
- Script to run: ./ops/smoke/tempo-check.sh --target current-canary
- Checks executed:
  * Health endpoints (service/health, model/kv-status) x 3 regions
  * Latency sample: 50 queries, median and p95
  * Error rate: count of 5xx in last 5m
  * Model checksum / version returned matches manifest
  * Simple golden generation comparison (3 prompts)
- Pass criteria: no health endpoint > WARN, median latency within gate, error delta within limit, no version mismatch.

Rollback decision matrix (simple):
- Trigger: latency p95 > baseline *1.5 OR error delta > 1% absolute OR queue depth > hard cap OR OOMs observed
- Action: immediate traffic flip back to previous stable variant, keep logs and metrics, open post-mortem ticket JIRA-RLX-4123-rollback
- Who: release lead + on-call SRE execute. Notify customer success if any customer-affecting metric triggered.

Operational scripts & one-line commands (for on-call laptop use):
- Snapshot metrics: ./ops/tools/snap-metrics.sh --query "service:latency,p95" --output /tmp/tempo-snap.json
- Promote canary: rcli promote --subset canary --percent 50
- Revert to stable: rcli revert --to stable --note "auto-rollback due to gate failure"
- Tail logs for service: kubectl -n redwood logs -l app=inference --since=20m | grep -i error | head -n 200

Communication templates (post to #cutover-ops):
- Cutover start template:
  [CUTOVER] Starting tempo cutover for release-2026-11 by <owner>. T=0 now. Canary 5% being promoted. Monitor #cutover-ops.

- Rollback announcement:
  [ROLLBACK] Rolling back release-2026-11 to stable due to telemetry gate fail: <reason>. Reversion initiated by <owner>. Further updates in this thread.

Dry-run notes from 2026-10-22:
- Observations: the laptop smoke script relied on internal DNS that was flaky from home VPN; added fallback IPs to script.
- Change: reduced canary ramp aggressiveness from 30m->15m to match typical user sessions (improved detection speed)
- Action item: #1 - add test IPs and fallback credentials to ops vault (assigned Marco)

Open questions / decisions to surface:
- Should we add a short-lived synthetic for VIP customers during canary (status: under debate with CS).
- Do we standardize the 15 minute cadence or leave it adjustable per release size? Proposal: default 15m but allow lead override up to 60m.

Post-cutover checklist (T+90m -> T+360m):
- Validate downstream consumers (billing, alerting hooks) received expected events
- Keep an eye on error rate for 6 hours; auto-rollback window ends at T+90m but manual remediation may be needed later
- Schedule a lightweight incident review if any gate was tripped (owner to file notes in Confluence)

Appendix (cheat-sheet):
- Key contacts: Aisha Patel (release lead), Marco Chen (ops), Sofia Alvarez (SRE on-call)
- Short commands: see "Operational scripts" section above
- Important links: Confluence runbook (CONFLUENCE-RELEASE-2026-11), PR: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/987

Notes to self (rough):
- Add a tiny dashboard that surfaces canary vs stable latency ratios in one chart.
- Add a line in the smoke script that fetches model-weights md5 to detect accidental variant swaps.
- Consider making the tempo plan the default for midweek minor releases.

-- end of conductor notes --

(If you copy this into a Google doc: convert checklist lines into checkboxes and pin the runbook link to #cutover-ops so it's discoverable.)
